ev.mng_t_cangue.title: The cangue
ev.mng_t_cangue.text: A hostile clan fell upon the camp and carried you off. Round your neck they put a cangue - a heavy wooden collar that keeps your hands from reaching your mouth. Tonight they are feasting, the guard is alone and young, and the river is a hundred paces off.
ev.mng_t_cangue.river: Stun the guard and make for the river
ev.mng_t_cangue.river.success: You lie in the water, the cangue braced against the bank, while the pursuers beat the bushes. One of them sees you - and says nothing. Later he seeks you out himself and becomes your friend and protector.
ev.mng_t_cangue.river.failure: They fish you out at dawn. Now you are their bondsman.
ev.mng_t_cangue.ransom: Wait for your kin to ransom you
ev.mng_t_cangue.ransom.ok: Your kin drive over most of the herd to ransom you. You are home, but the camp is poorer.
ev.mng_t_cangue.serve.ok: The cangue comes off. You carry water and argal in a stranger's yurt.
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.title: Without a herd
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.text: In a single night raiders have driven off almost all your livestock. On the steppe a man without a herd is nobody: no kumis, no felt, no bride-price. You are left with a yurt, a bow and a couple of sheep.
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.pursue.success: After five days you catch them by the Kherlen and drive back your own and some of theirs.
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.pursue.failure: The chase ends in an ambush. You come back without a horse and without hope.
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.batrak.ok: You herd others' flocks for a share of the young. Every lamb is a step back towards a yurt of your own.
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.patron: Put yourself under a rich noyan
ev.mng_t_herd_lost.patron.ok: The noyan gives you a flock to graze - and your loyalty now belongs to him.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.title: A wounded man at the well
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.text: By a dried-up well lies a wounded rider in a rich deel, his horse beside him lame. By the tamga on the harness he is of the khan's clan. Enemies may be on his trail.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.help: Give him water and hide him
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.help.success: For three days you hide him in a wagon of wool. He turns out to be a noyan, and he takes you among his nökers.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.help.failure: The pursuers find you both. They take him away, and beat you and leave you.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan.pass.ok: Another's trouble is not yours. You spur your horse on.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan_later.title: The noyan remembers
ev.mng_t_water_noyan_later.text: The noyan you once saved at the well names you before the khan at the kurultai. You are granted a hundred to command.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan_later.accept.ok: Now you hold a centurion's paiza with a hundred riders at your back.
ev.mng_t_water_noyan_later.decline.ok: You ask to stay with the noyan. He is moved.
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.title: Accused under the yasa
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.text: A neighbour you have long been at odds with has told the darughachi that you harboured a runaway slave. By the yasa the penalty is death. There are no witnesses - only his word against yours.
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.oath.success: You swear the most terrible oath of the steppe, stepping over a dog cut in two. The darughachi believes you.
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.oath.failure: The darughachi does not believe you. Your life is spared, but the fine ruins your household.
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.flee.ok: You slip away into the night with your family. In the new place no one knows your name.
ev.mng_t_false_accuse.pay.ok: Silver opens any ears. The case is closed, and your neighbour watches you with a smirk.
ev.mng_t_treasure.title: Silver in a mound
ev.mng_t_treasure.text: A storm has washed away part of an old mound, and from the sand a rotted sack has emerged - full of silver sükhe ingots and Chinese coins. Someone must have hidden his spoils after a city was taken and never come back.
ev.mng_t_treasure.keep.success: You split the silver into a hundred parts and spend it little by little. No one guesses.
ev.mng_t_treasure.keep.failure: The neighbour's son saw you digging. You had to hand almost all of it to the noyan - and explain yourself besides.
ev.mng_t_treasure.noyan.ok: The noyan lets you keep a quarter and remembers your honesty.
ev.mng_t_treasure.ovoo: Leave it: it belongs to the dead
ev.mng_t_treasure.ovoo.ok: You cover the sack again and set a stone on top. The spirits must be pleased.
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.title: Disgrace
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.text: Your noyan turned out to back the prince who lost at the kurultai. The new khan is purging the ulus: those loyal to their old lord lose their herds, sometimes their lives. Word reaches you: name his treasons, and you will keep what you have.
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.loyal.success: The khan is said to have remarked: "One who is loyal to his lord in misfortune will be loyal to me." You are spared and remembered.
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.loyal.failure: Your herds are given to others, and you are driven from the camp with a single yurt.
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.denounce.ok: You tell what you knew, and even what you did not. The silver comes. Sleep does not.
ev.mng_t_noyan_fall.flee.ok: You lead your people off to another ulus before anyone remembers you.
ev.mng_t_freed.title: A darkhan
ev.mng_t_freed.text: In a blizzard you alone led your master's herd out of a ravine and saved more than a hundred horses. Before everyone, your master declares you a darkhan - free, exempt from taxes, "until you have offended nine times".
ev.mng_t_freed.stay_near.ok: Your former master gives you three mares to breed from. A yurt of your own, a fire of your own.
ev.mng_t_freed.go_home: Go and look for your homeland
ev.mng_t_freed.go_home.ok: You leave with little. Somewhere out there is the land you were taken from as a child.
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.title: A raid at dawn
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.text: At dawn strange riders burst out of the mist. The yurts are burning, horses plunge at their tethers, there are shouts in a foreign tongue all around. Captives are being driven off with the herds.
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.fight.success: You fight free and lead people to the river. The raiders leave with little.
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.fight.failure: A lasso snaps round your neck. Now you are in a strange camp - a captive.
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.hide.success: You lie in the reeds until evening. The herd is gone, but you are free.
ev.mng_t_raid_captive.hide.failure: The dogs find you. You are taken with the others.
ev.mng_t_raid_late.title: The Oirats are coming
ev.mng_t_raid_late.text: The steppe is at war with itself again: the western Mongols, the Oirats, and the eastern khans are cutting each other down for power. Yesterday a lookout saw smoke beyond the pass; today hundreds of riders are already there.
ev.mng_t_raid_late.fight.success: You hold the ford until the noyan arrives. The Oirats ride off west.
ev.mng_t_raid_late.fight.failure: The Oirats break through. You live, but the herd is nearly gone.
ev.mng_t_raid_late.flee.ok: You abandon half the herd and go up into the mountains with your family.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.title: Carried off
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.text: The Merkits struck by night, and {npc} could not get away - {g=npc_sex:he was|she was} carried off to their camp three passes away. So too was Börte, young Temüjin's wife, taken once - and he won her back with the help of his anda and the khan of the Kereits.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.rescue.success: By night you slip into their camp and carry {npc} off on a single horse. They will sing of this.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.rescue.failure: You are spotted by the tethering posts. You barely get away, and {npc} remains there - for ever.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.allies.success: Three hundred riders scatter the Merkit camp. {npc} is back in your yurt.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.allies.failure: Your allies come too late: the Merkits have moved off beyond Baikal.
ev.mng_t_spouse_taken.mourn.ok: You stand a long while by the empty bed. The steppe is cruel.
ev.mng_t_golden_paiza.title: The golden paiza
ev.mng_t_golden_paiza.text: The khan has granted you a golden paiza with a tiger's head - the sign of a governor. You are to be darughachi over a city, answerable for its census, its relay stations and its taxes. If you fail, you answer with your head.
ev.mng_t_golden_paiza.accept.ok: The paiza is heavy as a stone. The city meets you with bows and lowered eyes.
ev.mng_t_golden_paiza.refuse.ok: The khan smiles thinly and gives the paiza to another.
ev.mng_t_paiza_later.title: Arrears
ev.mng_t_paiza_later.text: The city has not gathered its taxes: there was pestilence and people fled. An inspector is riding from the court. You could squeeze out what is missing by force - or write honestly to the khan as things are.
ev.mng_t_paiza_later.force.ok: The taxes are gathered. The city curses your name.
ev.mng_t_paiza_later.honest.success: The khan defers the tax for a year. In the city they bless you.
ev.mng_t_paiza_later.honest.failure: The paiza is taken back. You are a mere nöker again.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.title: The Black Death
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.text: A pestilence has come from the east along the caravan roads: swellings rise on people's bodies and in three days they are gone. In Sarai the dead are buried by the hundred each day. Khan Janibek's army besieging Caffa is melting away before your eyes.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.steppe: Get away into the far steppe
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.steppe.success: In the distant pastures the plague does not find you.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.steppe.failure: The plague catches you even on the steppe - it must have travelled with you.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.stay.success: You nurse three neighbours back to health and do not fall ill yourself.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.stay.failure: On the fourth day a swelling rises under your arm.
ev.mng_t_plague_caffa.note: In 1346 the army of Janibek, khan of the Golden Horde, was besieging Genoese Caffa in the Crimea when plague broke out in its ranks. According to Gabriele de' Mussi, corpses were hurled over the walls. From Caffa the pestilence travelled by ship to Constantinople, Italy and the whole of Europe.
ev.mng_t_khan_daughter.title: Güregen
ev.mng_t_khan_daughter.text: For your service the khan has decided to give you a princess of the Golden Lineage. A khan's son-in-law - a güregen - stands above any noyan, but lives under the eyes of the whole court. To refuse the khan is a mortal insult.
ev.mng_t_khan_daughter.accept.ok: The wedding lasts nine days. Now you are a güregen; everyone bows to you, and you bow to your wife.
ev.mng_t_khan_daughter.refuse.success: The khan believes in your vow and even praises your fidelity to your word.
ev.mng_t_khan_daughter.refuse.failure: The khan does not believe you. You are flogged and stripped of half your herds.
